pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text:
`greeks_based_pnl_explain` answers "how much of this period's P&L do the Greeks account for?" It takes your portfolio's `delta`, `gamma`, `vega`, `theta` and `rho`, plus the realised moves and the `actual_pnl`. It then gives a predicted P&L from a second-order expansion, and the unexplained residual is `actual_pnl` minus that prediction.

`pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` answers a different question: "does the model-based P&L track the full-revaluation P&L well enough to pass the FRTB test?" It takes two daily series, `risk_theoretical_pnl` and `hypothetical_pnl`. It evaluates their Spearman rank correlation together with the ratio of their standard deviations, then assigns a Basel traffic-light zone. The thresholds are set by the Basel Committee and are not parameters you can change.

In short, the first function explains one period's P&L from the Greeks, while the second tests whether two P&L series agree over time.

explain.text: `greeks_based_pnl_explain` (Greeks Based Pnl Explain) does a second-order Greeks P&L explain: it takes your portfolio's `delta`, `gamma`, `vega`, `theta` and `rho` along with the realised moves in the underlying (`spot_move`), volatility (`vol_move`), time (`time_step`) and rates (`rate_move`). From these it builds a predicted P&L: delta times the spot move, plus half gamma times the squared spot move, plus the vega, theta and rho terms. It then compares that with the `actual_pnl` you supply. The difference, actual minus predicted, is the unexplained residual, which is the quantity the FRTB P&L attribution test (PAT) scrutinises. Keep `theta` in the same time unit as `time_step`.

when.text:
`greeks_based_pnl_explain` fits when you want to see how much of a period's P&L your Greeks account for.

- You have portfolio `delta`, `gamma`, `vega`, `theta` and `rho`, plus the realised moves in the underlying, volatility, time and rates, and want a second-order Greeks-based predicted P&L.
- You have an observed (hypothetical) P&L for the period and want the unexplained residual, which is `actual_pnl` minus the predicted figure.
- You are looking at the quantity the FRTB P&L attribution test (PAT) scrutinises, and want to see where a gap comes from.
- You want a single, simple view that combines all the Greek components rather than examining them one at a time.
- For the formal FRTB test itself, `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` is listed as the Spearman correlation and ratio test.
